title: INT8/FP8 pilot - signal attenuation & rollback playbook
next_steps: Redwood to run 48-hour live A/B with INT8 blend and send raw logs
Customer to provide 200-edge-case prompts for regression hunt by Fri 2026-10-02
Schedule on-prem checklist call (private deployment) w/ security + infra next week
action_items: Priya Nair; run second-pass KV cache priming test and share perf sheet; 2026-10-03

summary: Weekly POC sync for Clarion HealthTech focused on quantization pilot. Reviewed INT8 and FP8 perf deltas, surfaced small but meaningful quality regressions on clinical extraction prompts. Agreed to run extended A/B with logging, tighten canary thresholds, and prepare rollback playbook for production readiness.
topics: perf deltas (latency/throughput), quality regressions (NER/clinical extraction), KV cache priming, canary/rollback playbook, telemetry retention and SLOs
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Liam Hart (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (SE), Carlos Mendes (SE), Evan Brooks (Clarion), Dr. Anita Rao (Clarion), Samir Patel (Clarion), Jules Kim (Clarion)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone good afternoon thanks for hopping on, quick agenda — perf readouts, quality deltas, and the rollback playbook we promised last week.
[00:23] Evan: Thanks Liam, we ran the week-one batches on dev and saw the latency drop like you said but, um, some of the entity extraction is missing tokens, especially in the oncology dataset.
[01:05] Priya: Right — so high level numbers first: FP8 gave us ~12% token-cost reduction and INT8 blend (selective layers) showed ~28% reduction; p95 latency improved by ~10-15% across our test harness. These are median values across mixed short/long prompt mixes.
[02:10] Dr. Anita: The problem is the SNR on the oncology NER cases — model returns shorter spans or drops protein names. It's subtle but fails our downstream mapper.
[03:05] Carlos: We looked at perplexity and SNR per prompt bucket — low-frequency tokens are where the attenuation happens. Might be quantization scale factors + KV cache priming interacting.
[03:52] Samir: For infra side, CPU/GPU utilization is fine but we saw more mem copies on INT8 path — could be our CUDA kernel choice on the node. Also want to flag that our on-prem setup uses older drivers so results might differ vs hosted.
[05:20] Jules: Timeline wise we need a production rollback plan before we roll to canary — legal needs assurance.
[06:12] Liam: Agreed. We put together a rollback playbook draft, it's not final. Today we want to validate thresholds and the automated failover triggers.
[07:00] Priya: Quick note on methodology: we ran two variants — full-FP8 (end-to-end) and blended INT8 (embedding + decoder layers float fused). The blended approach seems to keep more fidelity but less cost saving.
[08:18] Evan: Any idea what causes the named-entity truncation? Missed tokens rather than wrong label.
[08:45] Priya: Likely attenuation in logits for rare tokens after quantization; for FP8 we saw less truncation but a few hallucinations in long contexts.
[09:30] Dr. Anita: We also observed differences when KV cache priming was disabled; with priming the outputs match baseline much better.
[10:05] Carlos: So an operational knob is priming the positional KV or prewarm sequences for known common prefixes — that reduced the delta by ~60% in our test.
[11:40] Evan: Okay that's promising. Can you share exact priming sequence? We prefer deterministic scripts.
[12:05] Priya: We'll push the priming config and a short script to the shared drive — it includes prefix lengths and token cutoff heuristics.
[13:30] Samir: Regarding rollback, we need both automatic and manual — auto for confidence bands outside acceptance, manual for security signoff. How does Redwood recommend canary thresholds?
[14:10] Liam: We recommend dual thresholds: 1) telemetry based (SNR drop > 7% or NER F1 drop > 3% over 1 hour) triggers auto-failover; 2) escalation band where product/security gets paged if the drop persists 30 minutes. Playbook will include steps to rollforward and roll back to previous quant profile.
[15:40] Jules: What about data retention and logs — legal asked for 90 day retention on request logs for audits.
[16:10] Carlos: We can set telemetry retention to 90 days for the pilot; also we can push redaction hooks to drop PHI tokens before storage. Need confirmation on redaction rules.
[17:05] Dr. Anita: We'll send a redaction spec. Also need to confirm SOC2 artifacts for on-prem deployment.
[18:00] Liam: Noted. Next, perf deltas — Priya can you walk through the p50/p95 table?
[18:22] Priya: Sure — p50: baseline 85ms -> INT8 blend 72ms -> FP8 75ms. p95: baseline 420ms -> INT8 blend 360ms -> FP8 370ms. Throughput increased ~18% for batch sizes used.
[19:45] Evan: Those are helpful, cost numbers?
[20:10] Priya: Estimated token cost reduction per 1M tokens: FP8 ~12%, INT8 blend ~28% — caveat: inference time cost savings depend on kernel availability and run-time mem copies.
[21:30] Samir: Could we see microbenchmark traces? We need the NVTX spans.
[22:05] Carlos: Yes we'll attach NVTX traces and the per-layer timing. Expect some noise from our older driver stack.
[23:00] Dr. Anita: On quality regression, can we do targeted retraining or calibration? We want to avoid full finetune.
[23:40] Priya: Options: 1) calibrate quant scales per-layer with a small calibration dataset; 2) selective float fallback for attention layers critical to entity recall; 3) KV cache priming. Calibration reduced the NER drop in our tests.
[25:10] Evan: We ran a small calibration and saw improvements but not perfect. What's the cost of selective fallback?
[25:30] Carlos: Selective fallback increases token-cost by ~6-8% vs pure INT8 but halves the regression delta. It's a tradeoff.
[26:00] Jules: Let's quantify acceptance: NER F1 can't drop more than 2% absolute. If we exceed, rollback.
[26:30] Liam: Noted — set 2% absolute as acceptance criteria. We'll wire that into canary checks.
[27:15] Samir: About the extended A/B you mentioned — how long to run?
[27:40] Priya: We propose 48-72 hours with live traffic mirrored 10% to A and 90% to baseline, with full logging of tokens and NVTX traces sampled. That should give enough data on low-frequency tokens.
[28:35] Evan: OK do that. Also need a list of top 500 user queries to seed priming.
[29:05] Dr. Anita: We'll extract and sanitize the queries by Thursday.
[30:10] Liam: Good. Quick note on canary implementation — Redwood will provide a rollout config that supports percentage traffic ramps, auto-fail thresholds, and region-aware fallbacks.
[31:00] Carlos: Also adding a soft-threshold band where we throttle quant profile gradually rather than hard switch reduces spike risk. We call it ramped attenuation.
[31:40] Priya: On the telemetry side, we'll add per-prompt SNR and NER F1 sampling and a regression alert that flags specific prompt clusters.
[33:15] Evan: Could you filter the telemetry to only show de-identified tokens? Legal doesn't want PHI in logs.
[33:45] Carlos: We'll apply token hashing and redaction hooks before sending logs to observability.
[34:20] Dr. Anita: One weird thing — in one test the FP8 run produced a longer answer that actually improved recall but introduced hallucinated medications. Strange.
[35:05] Priya: Yeah FP8 can change generation dynamics; sometimes length increases and hallucination risk rises. We'll add hallucination detectors to the pipeline.
[36:00] Jules: For the rollback playbook can you outline exact steps?
[36:20] Liam: Sure — 1) detect via telemetry -> 2) auto-reduce traffic to 0% for quant profile -> 3) switch to baseline model variant -> 4) re-run quick smoke tests (10 synthetic prompts) -> 5) if pass, re-escalate; else open incident and notify product/security. We'll draft exact commands for both hosted and on-prem.
[38:05] Samir: Commands for on-prem need sudo kube creds; we'll coordinate who runs them.
[38:40] Carlos: We'll include runbook entries with required IAM roles and the minimal-kill sequence.
[39:10] Evan: Anything about cost forecasting during canary? We need estimated cost delta on 10% traffic.
[39:50] Priya: Rough: if INT8 blend is used on 10% traffic, expect ~2.8% total cost reduction overall; FP8 at 10% yields ~1.2%. But varies by sequence length.
[40:30] Dr. Anita: For acceptance we'll need per-endpoint SLOs defined. NER F1 >= baseline-2% and p95 latency not worse than baseline+25ms (or rollback).
[41:10] Liam: We'll capture those SLOs in the canary config.
[42:00] Priya: Quick note — kernel mismatch on some GPUs caused extra memcpy which hurt INT8 perf on your driver. We recommend driver upgrade or use of dedicated nodes with verified kernels for production.
[43:05] Samir: Driver upgrade will take time; can Redwood provide a compatibility matrix?
[43:30] Carlos: Yes, compatibility doc will be attached.
[44:00] Evan: Any competitor approaches? Anthropic recommended model-splitting and fallback; OpenAI suggests adaptive sampling. We discussed those but prefer Redwood's selective-fallback approach.
[45:10] Priya: We can also try temperature annealing and length penalties as a mitigation for hallucination if needed.
[46:00] Jules: Okay, let's recap next steps.
[46:15] Liam: Recap: Redwood -> run 48hr A/B with NVTX and priming script; share priming script + compatibility matrix + rollback playbook draft by Monday. Clarion -> send 200 edge-case prompts + top-500 queries list by Thursday; confirm redaction rules. Both -> sync on 2026-10-06 for playbook review.
[47:20] Dr. Anita: Sounds good. One last question: what's the expected delta in throughput if we enable selective fallback?
[48:00] Priya: Throughput drops a bit vs pure INT8 — expect 6-9% less throughput but throughput still better than baseline in most batch regimes.
[48:45] Samir: For our SLA we need p95 under 500ms; these numbers are promising if driver issues resolved.
[49:30] Liam: Great. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[50:00] [meeting continues with checklist walk; end of recorded transcript snippet to match duration]

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors — e.g., 'attenuation' misheard as 'atten shoe ation' in one segment, speaker overlap at 00:23, occasional proper noun misspellings.

Attachments referenced: /drive/clarion/priming_script_v2.sh, /drive/clarion/nvtx_traces.zip, rollback_playbook_draft_v0.3.pdf
